chunks: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Abd al-Malik al-Qummi came to him and said: 'May God keep you well! Can I drink water while standing?' He said to him: 'If you so desire.' He said: 'Shall I drink in one breath until I am quenched?' He said: 'If you so desire.' He said: 'May I prostrate with my hands inside my garment?' He said: 'If you so desire.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By God, it is not from this and the likes of it that I fear for you.'

key_terms.أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ: A polite address meaning 'May God keep you well' or 'May God correct you,' used in classical Arabic as a respectful way to preface a question to a religious authority
key_terms.إِنْ شِئْتَ: If you so desire/wish — a phrase indicating permission without compulsion
key_terms.شِبْهِهِ: The likes of it, similar matters — indicating the Imam's concern extends beyond just these three examples

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to drink water while standing in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a conversation between a companion named Abd al-Malik al-Qummi and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in which the companion asks about three practices: drinking water while standing, drinking in one breath until quenched, and prostrating with hands inside clothing. The Imam permits all three with the phrase 'if you so desire,' indicating their permissibility. The Imam then delivers a profound pastoral statement, emphasizing by oath that these minor behavioral matters are not what he truly fears for his followers — implying his deeper concern lies with spiritual and moral failures rather than such secondary rulings.
